newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland soon to call tender for Pekao sale adviser.
newsitem.headline: Poland soon to call tender for Pekao sale adviser.

text.p: Poland will soon announce a tender for adviser in the privatisation of Bank Pekao SA, whose public offering of 15 percent of shares is seen in the first half of 1998, the bank's president said on Friday.

"The Treasury Ministry will soon announce a tender for adviser on the privatisation of the group. If that happens, there's a big chance that in the first half of 1998 we will become a public bank," Andrzej Dorosz told a news conference.
Dorosz did not say when the tender might be called but said it was in the best interest of the bank if the adviser was chosen as soon as possible. @
The government's privatisation plan estimates the bank's value at three billion to 4.5 billion zlotys. It foresees another 15 percent of shares going to employees for free.
Dorosz said he did not rule out that the bank would gain a stragegic investor in the second part of its privatisation but said it was too early to give the timing.

The Bank Pekao SA group formed last year after the state treasury lumped together with Bank Pekao SA Pomorski Bank Kredytowy W Szczecinie SA (PBKS), Powszechny Bank Gospodarczy SA (PGS) and Bank Depozytowo-Kredytowy SA (BDK). @
The group made a 322.2-million-zloty net profit in this year's first half against 514 million zlotys for all of 1996.

Dorosz said parent Bank Pekao SA, which lifted first-half net profit to 171.3 million zlotys from 144.2 million in the same period last year, should beat the 247.5-million zloty net profit for all of last year.

Dorosz said the central bank's lifting of obligatory reserves this year had negatively affected its earnings but that the bank, whose physical plant was insured, should not be damaged by the current flooding in Poland.
